extracted.intended_audience: researchers (including early-career and historically excluded researchers) interested in reviewing or requesting reviews of preprints and datasets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and platform features for conducting and requesting open, constructive peer reviews of preprints (and datasets), including collaborative formats and training to build reviewing skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open preprint reviews (openness & accessibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open preprint reviews for all researchers — providing and receiving feedback on preprints from an international community of peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site emphasizes that reviews are open and available to all researchers; actions include 'Review a preprint' and 'Request a review' to participate in the open-review ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide and receive constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be constructive — aimed at improving the work through actionable, respectful critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The homepage repeatedly frames the service as a place to 'Provide and receive constructive feedback' and highlights published PREreviews as examples; the emphasis is on useful, improvement-focused comments rather than unhelpful criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be provided in a timely manner to ensure preprints receive prompt community feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PREreview Clubs are described specifically as groups where 'members work together to provide timely, constructive feedback', implying timeliness is a core expectation of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative and interactive review formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Use collaborative, interactive review processes (e.g., Live Reviews and PREreview Clubs) as alternatives to or supplements for traditional peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live Reviews are described as 'collaborative, interactive preprint review calls' and PREreview Clubs enable group review work. The framing encourages real-time discussion, co‑authored reviews, and community engagement rather than isolated single-author reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review training and skill development
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer training (interactive workshops) to help researchers hone their peer review skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site offers 'Peer review training' and 'Interactive workshops for organizations and institutions looking to help their members hone their skills as reviewers', indicating that reviewers are expected to develop competencies through structured training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and empowerment of underserved and early-career researchers (inclusivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively support, empower, and create opportunities for diverse and historically excluded communities of researchers — particularly early-career researchers — to participate in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mission statement explicitly states support for underserved researchers to 'find a voice, train, and engage in peer review', which implies programmatic efforts and norms to lower barriers and center inclusivity in review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing datasets as part of open review practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Include datasets in the scope of review activity — users can 'Review a dataset' in addition to preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site lists 'Review a dataset' as a primary action, signaling that evaluation of data resources (not just manuscript text) is part of the platform's standards for reproducibility and openness; no detailed dataset-evaluation criteria are provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative to traditional peer review (experimentation with process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote experimental, community-driven approaches to peer review that differ from traditional journal-managed review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through Live Reviews, Clubs, open publishing of PREreviews, and training, the platform encourages community-led, transparent workflows as viable alternatives to closed, editor-mediated peer review.
